statement_record.book: For a small category C, a presheaf on C is a contravariant set-valued functor on C, i.e. an object of the functor category Set^{C^op}.
statement_record.intree: Definition Presheaf (U C : Category) := U^op ⟶ C.  Definition Presheaves {U C : Category} := [U^op, C].
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, and in-tree strictly more general on two axes. (i) The value category is arbitrary (C), Riehl's case being C := Sets, which the library instantiates wherever it matters (Theory/Sheaf.v:192's Sheaf takes a Presheaf C Sets; Theory/Sheaf/Category.v works over Presheaves C Sets). (ii) SMALLNESS of the base is not required, and cannot be: the library tracks size by universe polymorphism (universes {o h p} on Category) rather than by a smallness predicate, so [U^op, C] is formed for any U at whatever universe level results. That is a generalization, not a weakening — every small C admits the construction. The contravariance is literal (U^op via Construction/Opposite.v, where C^op^op = C by reflexivity), and the covariant variant is declared alongside as Copresheaf/Copresheaves (Theory/Sheaf.v:130,133).

statement_record.book: (1) A Grothendieck topos is cocomplete, so its defining adjunction can instead be produced from the composite of the reflector with the Yoneda embedding, the reflector being the left Kan extension of that functor on representables. (2) Every Grothendieck topos is an elementary topos. (3) The converse fails: Fin is an elementary topos that is not a Grothendieck topos, one reason being that it is neither complete nor cocomplete.
statement_record.intree: Definition FinSet_Topos : ElementaryTopos FinSet := {| topos_terminal := ...; topos_classifier := FinSet_Classifier |}.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the POSITIVE half of clause (3) is asserted — skeletal finite sets form an elementary topos, and with a computing witness (Pow 2 = 4 by eq_refl). Clauses (1) and (2), and the negative half of (3), have no in-tree counterpart. In-tree the elementary-topos class also carries finite limits explicitly as terminal + binary products + pullbacks (Structure/Topos.v:112-118), with the header at lines 22-25 disclosing that the pullback/equalizer reduction is not formalized; that is a presentational difference, not a weakening of what FinSet_Topos asserts.

gap: Clause (1) is entirely absent: Cocomplete exists only as a definition schema (Structure/Complete.v:119, `Definition Cocomplete {C : Category} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Colimit F`) with NO inhabitant anywhere — `grep -rn '@Cocomplete\|: Cocomplete' --include='*.v' .` finds only the definition itself and the hypothesis position in Theory/Adamek/Corollaries.v:61 — so 'a Grothendieck topos is cocomplete' cannot even be stated (there is no Grothendieck topos either, see riehl:E.4:def-grothendieck-topos), and the 'reflector = Lan along Yoneda' reformulation is missing: Theory/Kan/Extension.v:222 has the LeftKan class, but nothing connects it to the Yoneda embedding of Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v (`grep -rniF 'free cocompletion' --include='*.v' .` — 1 hit, prose only, Theory/Sheaf.v:117). statement_record.book: A site is a small category C equipped, for each object U, with a specified COLLECTION of covering families {U_i → U} of morphisms into U, these collections required to satisfy a weak pullback condition.
statement_record.intree: Class Site (C : Category) := { covering_family (u : C) := sigT (Vector.t (∃ uᵢ, uᵢ ~> u)); coverage (u : C) : covering_family u; coverage_condition ... : ∃ hs : covering_family v, ForallT (λ '(vⱼ; hⱼ), ExistsT (λ '(uᵢ; fᵢ), ∃ k, fᵢ ∘ k ≈ g ∘ hⱼ) (`2 fs)) (`2 hs) }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the data, faithful on the axiom. The axiom coverage_condition is exactly the weak/factorization form Riehl alludes to — given a covering family of u and any g : v ~> u there is a covering family of v each of whose legs composes with g so as to factor through some leg of the original — which is the classical coverage axiom and does NOT demand actual pullbacks, matching 'weak pullback condition'. The DATA is strictly weaker: coverage supplies ONE covering family per object rather than a collection of them, and each family is finite (a Vector.t), whereas Riehl's covering families are arbitrary. The in-tree comment at Theory/Sheaf.v:164-166 concedes this in so many words.

gap: Two concrete deficits. (1) Data: `coverage (u : C) : covering_family u` selects EXACTLY ONE covering family per object; a genuine coverage/Grothendieck topology assigns a collection (a Type or set of families) to each object, so the in-tree class cannot express 'U is covered by this family AND by that other one'. The file says so itself at Theory/Sheaf.v:164-166 ('less general than a full coverage'), as does Theory/Sheaf/Category.v:29-31. (2) Each covering family is a FINITE vector (sigT (Vector.t ...)), excluding infinite covers — the open covers of the motivating topological example are not in general finite. Additionally, no Site instance exists anywhere in the tree (`grep -rn 'Site' --include='*.v' .` yields only the class, its uses inside Theory/Sheaf.v, and the Context binder at Theory/Sheaf/Category.v:68), and smallness of C is not tracked (universe polymorphism instead of a smallness predicate — a generalization, not a defect).

evidence.intree_statement: Class Sheaf `{@Site C} (X : Presheaf C Sets) := { restriction : ∀ u : C, let '(i; f) := coverage u in ForallT (λ '(uᵢ; fᵢ), ∀ xᵢ : X uᵢ, (∀ (v : C) (g : v ~> uᵢ), ForallT (λ '(uⱼ; fⱼ), ∀ h : v ~> uⱼ, fᵢ ∘ g ≈ fⱼ ∘ h → ∀ xⱼ : X uⱼ, fmap[X] g xᵢ ≈ fmap[X] h xⱼ) f) → ∃! x : X u, fmap[X] fᵢ x ≈ xᵢ) f }.

statement_record.book: Taking C := O(X), the poset of opens of a space X, a presheaf P assigns a set P(U) to each open with restriction maps along inclusions; P is a SHEAF exactly when, for every open cover {U_α} of every open U, the fork P(U) → ∏_α P(U_α) ⇉ ∏_{α,β} P(U_α ∩ U_β) given by the two restrictions is an equalizer in Set.
statement_record.intree: Class Sheaf `{@Site C} (X : Presheaf C Sets) := { restriction : ∀ u : C, ... ∀ xᵢ : X uᵢ, (compatibility antecedent) → ∃! x : X u, fmap[X] fᵢ x ≈ xᵢ }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker, and materially so. The in-tree predicate is the abstract-site unique-gluing form (∃! x with prescribed restrictions), not the equalizer fork, and it is stated over the single chosen covering family of a Site rather than over all open covers. Worse, the library's own review (Theory/Sheaf/Category.v:32-42) establishes that the condition as written is not the textbook one even for that one family: the gluing clause is PER-LEG (one section over one uᵢ, not a simultaneous matching family), and the compatibility antecedent quantifies over ALL sections xⱼ of the other leg, so instantiating v := uᵢ, g := h := id and j := i forces xᵢ ≈ xⱼ for every xⱼ : X uᵢ — the hypothesis is satisfiable only when X uᵢ is a subsingleton, making the condition vacuous at any covered object with two inequivalent sections.

gap: Three separable deficits. (1) Presentation: the equalizer-fork formulation Riehl gives — the canonical fork into ∏_α P(U_α) ⇉ ∏_{α,β} P(U_α ∩ U_β) being an equalizer — is not stated; the in-tree condition is the element-level unique-gluing form, and no lemma relates the two (the library has Structure/Equalizer.v and Structure/Limit/Product.v but never assembles the sheaf fork). (2) Correctness: by the library's own analysis at Theory/Sheaf/Category.v:32-42 the in-tree gluing clause is per-leg and its compatibility antecedent is mis-quantified, so it is VACUOUS beyond subsingleton fibres; re-founding Sheaf on honest matching families is a named deferral (ledger entry 1, Theory/Sheaf/Category.v:46-47). (3) The motivating example is absent: there is no poset of opens O(X) and no topological space anywhere in the tree, hence no site instance to run the definition on.

Lemma cogenerator_canonical_monic {C : Category} (comp : @Complete C) (G : Cogenerator C) (c : C) : Monic (cogen_canonical comp G c).   (* proof consumes cog_separates directly: `apply (cog_separates G g1 g2); intros j k` — the separation content is genuinely in force, not inert *)

statement_record.book: A separating set for E is a set of objects that is jointly separating: for any parallel pair f ≠ g : B ⇉ A there is an object G in the set and a map h : G → B with f∘h ≠ g∘h. Equivalently the representables E(G,−) jointly reflect equality of morphisms.
statement_record.intree: Record Cogenerator {C : Category} := { cog_index : Type; cog_obj : cog_index -> C; cog_separates : forall (x y : C) (f g : x ~> y), (forall (j : cog_index) (k : y ~> cog_obj j), k ∘ f ≈ k ∘ g) -> f ≈ g }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker only by variance, and that gap is closable definitionally. What is declared is the DUAL notion — a family into which arrows out of the codomain jointly detect equality, i.e. the representables C(−, G_j) jointly faithful. Instantiating this same record at C^op yields Riehl's separating set on the nose, because Construction/Opposite.v:106-111 defines the opposite category with `hom x y := hom y x` and `compose f g := g ∘ f` DEFINITIONALLY: at C^op, `cog_separates` reads `forall (f g : y ~> x), (forall j (k : cog_obj j ~> y), f ∘ k ≈ g ∘ k) -> f ≈ g`, which is exactly the contrapositive of the book's condition. Modulo that instantiation the strength is identical, including the packaging of the family as an index Type (smallness supplied as data, as elsewhere in SAFT), and the in-tree form is stated as the contrapositive (agreement ⇒ equality) rather than with the existential.

gap: No in-tree definition, notation, or consumer names the covariant separating/generating set. Only the dual (Cogenerator) is declared, and it is used only in its dual role (Adjunction/SAFT.v builds the product of the cogenerating family and shows the canonical map into it monic). The library's own idiom for putting a dual notion in force is to DECLARE it at the opposite category — Structure/Initial.v (Initial C unfolds to Terminal (C^op)), Construction/Reflective.v:85 (Coreflective S := @Reflective (C^op) (op_subcategory S)), Comonad := @Monad (C^op) (M^op) — and that declaration is simply not made here, so `Cogenerator (C^op)` is a term a reader must form for himself; nothing in-tree ever does. Consequently no lemma about separating sets (in particular none of the roles Giraud's condition (vi) plays) exists, and there is no instance of a separating set for any concrete category.
